note: Outside on four of five. He is a salaried Learning & Development programme manager and former university lecturer, not a business owner or physician, and he has resigned with no replacement role — 'I'm not certain about my income after the 15th of October.' Income fails outright at a stated ceiling of €200 a month. Health is not the neglected corner of a good life, it is the emergency at the centre of it: diagnosed bulimia nervosa, autism, childhood PTSD, weekly suicidal ideation against a prior attempt, IBS with confirmed slow bowel transit, and a congenital condition that means he has never felt full. That is rescue, not good to great. The one criterion he clearly meets is the exclusion: he is not gym-averse and not sedentary — he walks over 300 km a month, plays volleyball, holds a gym membership and trained seriously with kettlebells from 15 to 19. Two observations for the rollup. First, the stated ICP has no clinical or psychiatric criterion, and it is the absence of that criterion, not the presence of any stated one, that should have stopped this call inside the first ten minutes. Second, on every non-clinical dimension of intent — discipline, self-knowledge, honesty, willingness to do the work — he is stronger than the prospects who buy, which is a straightforward pricing and packaging problem rather than a targeting one.
